_meta.description: Breakdown of the cost of moving value from CNY to USD. Split into (1) the compliance cost of a lawful conversion, (2) the tax cost of the underlying income event, and (3) the administrative and criminal penalty exposure of an unlawful route, quantified from published official cases.
_meta.arithmetic_note: Percentages in the case table are computed as fine divided by amount moved and are shown ONLY where both official figures are expressed in the same currency. Where the amount moved is in USD, CAD or HKD and the fine is in RMB, the percentage is left null because computing it would require an exchange rate that is not fixed by any source in this register. No rate has been assumed.

headline_finding.title: China levies no tax on the act of converting CNY into USD
headline_finding.body: Nothing in the Individual Income Tax Law, the Enterprise Income Tax Law, the Regulation on Foreign Exchange Administration, the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange or the Detailed Rules imposes a tax, levy or conversion charge on exchanging renminbi for foreign currency. The obstacle the user describes as a 'considerable amount of taxes' is not a conversion tax. It is one of three different things, and separating them is the whole analysis.

components.name: Tax on the underlying income or gain event
components.detail: Individual income tax at 3% to 45% on comprehensive income, 5% to 35% on business income and 20% on interest, dividends, property leasing, property transfer and incidental income; enterprise income tax at 25%; withholding at 10% on dividends, interest and royalties paid to a non-resident. This tax is owed because the income arose, not because the money moved, and it is owed whether or not the funds ever leave China. Art.15 of the Individual Income Tax Law makes the tax-paid certificate a precondition to registering a transfer of real property or of equity, and Art.13(1) of the Detailed Rules makes a tax voucher a precondition to an overseas individual converting earned income.

components.name: Foreign exchange control, not tax
components.detail: The constraint on moving money out is quantitative and documentary, not fiscal. Art.9 of the Measures applies annual total-amount management of USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year to individual FX settlement and to domestic-individual FX purchase. Art.13 lets an overseas individual convert legitimate current-account income with no stated annual ceiling. Capital-account items require SAFE approval or registration. Art.5 of the Regulation states that the State does not restrict current-account international payments and transfers, which is why the lawful routes cluster in the current account.

components.name: Commercial cost of the conversion itself
components.nature: Real but small, and not fixed by regulation
components.detail: The bank's buy-sell spread and its remittance charge are set commercially by each bank. No instrument in this register fixes a retail conversion spread, so no percentage is stated here. The Regulation at Art.27 provides only for a managed floating exchange rate based on market supply and demand. This component is flagged rather than quantified.

cost_layers.name: Chinese tax on the income event
cost_layers.applies_to: Every route, because the tax arises on the income, not on the remittance

verified_rates.item: Wages and comprehensive income of a resident individual
Wages of a non-resident individual, per month
verified_rates.rate: 3% to 45% on revenue less RMB 5,000

verified_rates.item: Remuneration for personal services and royalties of a non-resident, per item
verified_rates.rate: 20% on 80% of revenue, an effective 16%

verified_rates.item: Dividends received by an individual
verified_rates.rate: 20% on the full amount of each receipt

verified_rates.item: Gain on transfer of property by an individual
verified_rates.rate: 20% on revenue less original value and reasonable expenses

verified_rates.item: Business income of an individual
Enterprise income tax on a resident enterprise
Withholding on dividends, interest and royalties paid to a non-resident enterprise
Withholding on a non-resident enterprise's gain on property transfer
verified_rates.rate: 10% on gross revenue less net value of the property

verified_rates.item: VAT on sale of services, intangibles and financial products
Insurance indemnity received by an individual
verified_rates.rate: Exempt

cost_layers.name: Treaty relief
cost_layers.applies_to: US recipients of Chinese-source dividends, interest, royalties and gains

verified_rates.item: Dividends, treaty cap
verified_rates.rate: 10% of the gross dividend

verified_rates.item: Interest, treaty cap
verified_rates.rate: 10% of the gross interest

verified_rates.item: Royalties, treaty cap
verified_rates.rate: 10% of the gross royalty

verified_rates.item: Leasing of industrial, commercial or scientific equipment
verified_rates.rate: Taxed on 70% of the gross amount, an effective cap of 7%

verified_rates.item: Net benefit of the treaty on these items
verified_rates.rate: Zero
verified_rates.note: Because the domestic reduced rate under Art.91 of the Chinese EIT Implementation Regulations is also 10%, the treaty cap produces no reduction. The treaty's real value to a US person is Art.22, the foreign tax credit, not a lower withholding rate.

cost_layers.name: US tax on the same income
cost_layers.applies_to: Every route, because a US citizen is taxed on worldwide income

verified_rates.item: Scope
verified_rates.rate: Worldwide income, regardless of where the funds are held

verified_rates.item: Relief option A - foreign earned income exclusion
Relief option A - foreign housing limitation
Relief option B - foreign tax credit limitation
verified_rates.rate: US tax liability multiplied by foreign-source taxable income over total taxable income

verified_rates.item: Relief option B - carryback and carryover
verified_rates.rate: 1 year back, 10 years forward

verified_rates.item: Relief option B - de minimis election, no Form 1116
verified_rates.rate: Creditable foreign tax of USD 300, or USD 600 on a joint return

verified_rates.item: Constraint - no stacking
verified_rates.rate: No credit or deduction for foreign tax paid on income excluded under the foreign earned income or housing exclusions

verified_rates.item: Conversion and remittance of already-taxed funds
verified_rates.rate: No further US income tax
verified_rates.note: Moving after-tax money between the taxpayer's own accounts is not a realisation event. Publication 54 requires only that amounts be expressed in US dollars, translated from the functional currency.

cost_layers.name: US reporting obligations and their penalties
cost_layers.applies_to: Holding the Chinese account at all, independently of any remittance

verified_rates.item: FBAR threshold
verified_rates.rate: Aggregate foreign financial accounts above USD 10,000 at any time in the year

verified_rates.item: FBAR non-willful penalty
verified_rates.rate: Statutory USD 10,000; adjusted maximum USD 16,536

verified_rates.item: FBAR willful penalty
verified_rates.rate: Statutory USD 100,000; adjusted maximum USD 165,353, with the statute also providing for up to 50% of the account balance

verified_rates.item: General willful Bank Secrecy Act penalty
verified_rates.rate: Statutory USD 25,000 to USD 100,000; adjusted USD 71,545 to USD 286,184

verified_rates.item: Funds-transfer recordkeeping violation
verified_rates.rate: Statutory USD 10,000; adjusted USD 26,262

verified_rates.item: Form 8938 threshold, single or MFS living in the US
verified_rates.rate: Above USD 50,000 at year end or USD 75,000 at any time

verified_rates.item: Form 8938 threshold, MFJ living in the US
verified_rates.rate: Above USD 100,000 at year end or USD 150,000 at any time

verified_rates.item: Form 8938 threshold, single or MFS living abroad
verified_rates.rate: Above USD 200,000 at year end or USD 300,000 at any time

verified_rates.item: Form 8938 threshold, MFJ living abroad
verified_rates.rate: Above USD 400,000 at year end or USD 600,000 at any time

verified_rates.item: FinCEN Form 105 threshold for moving cash across the US border
verified_rates.rate: More than USD 10,000 at one time

verified_rates.item: Automatic information flow from Chinese banks to the IRS
verified_rates.rate: None established
verified_rates.note: China is recorded on the US Treasury FATCA register as 'Agreement in Substance', Model 1, treated as in effect from 30 June 2014, with no signed agreement. There is therefore no executed intergovernmental agreement under which Chinese financial institutions report automatically to the IRS, and the compliance burden sits entirely on the taxpayer's own filings.

cost_layers.name: Chinese administrative penalties, if the route is not compliant

verified_rates.item: Evading FX supervision: transferring domestic FX abroad, or transferring domestic capital abroad by deceit (Art.39)
verified_rates.rate: Order to repatriate within a time limit plus a fine of up to 30% of the evaded amount; in serious circumstances 30% to 100%; criminal liability where a crime is constituted

verified_rates.item: Illegal FX arbitrage, including fraudulent purchase of FX on false or invalid documents (Art.40)
verified_rates.rate: Order to re-exchange plus a fine of up to 30% of the illegal amount; in serious circumstances 30% to 100%

verified_rates.item: Carrying FX across the border in violation of the rules (Art.42)
verified_rates.rate: Warning plus a fine of up to 20% of the illegal amount

verified_rates.item: Unauthorised change of the use of FX or of settled FX funds (Art.44)
verified_rates.rate: Correction, confiscation of illegal gains and a fine of up to 30%; in serious circumstances 30% to 100%

verified_rates.item: Private, disguised or intermediary buying and selling of FX (Art.45)
verified_rates.rate: Warning, confiscation of illegal gains and a fine of up to 30% of the illegal amount; in serious circumstances 30% to 100%; criminal liability where a crime is constituted

verified_rates.item: Failure to declare balance-of-payments statistics, or submitting untrue documents (Art.48)
verified_rates.rate: Correction and warning; up to RMB 300,000 for an institution and up to RMB 50,000 for an individual

verified_rates.item: Breach of the Detailed Rules not otherwise specified
verified_rates.rate: Art.39 of the Detailed Rules provided fines of up to RMB 30,000 for a bank and RMB 1,000 for an individual, but that article was abolished by Huifa [2023] No.8 Annex 3

verified_rates.item: Collateral consequence
verified_rates.rate: Placement on the SAFE watch list and entry of the penalty into the PBOC credit-reference system

cost_layers.name: Chinese criminal exposure, if the route is unlawful
cost_layers.applies_to: Underground banking and disguised FX dealing

verified_rates.item: Offence
verified_rates.rate: Illegal business operation, Criminal Law Art.225(4)

verified_rates.item: Serious circumstances
verified_rates.rate: Illegal business amount of RMB 5,000,000 or more, or illegal gains of RMB 100,000 or more

verified_rates.item: Serious circumstances at a reduced threshold
verified_rates.rate: RMB 2,500,000 or more, or illegal gains of RMB 50,000 or more, together with a prior criminal prosecution, an administrative penalty within two years, refusal to disclose where the funds went, or other serious consequences

verified_rates.item: Especially serious circumstances
verified_rates.rate: Illegal business amount of RMB 25,000,000 or more, or illegal gains of RMB 500,000 or more

verified_rates.item: Deemed illegal gains where they cannot be determined
verified_rates.rate: One thousandth of the illegal business amount, with a fine of one to five times that amount

verified_rates.item: Conversion of the offence amount
verified_rates.rate: Computed in RMB at the central parity rate published by the China Foreign Exchange Trade System or a PBOC-authorised institution on the date of discovery

observations.finding: Where both figures are in RMB, published fines for illegal FX dealing through underground banks cluster tightly at 7%, 8% and 12% of the amount moved.
observations.significance: These sit well inside the Art.45 statutory band of up to 30%, and far below the 30% to 100% band reserved for serious circumstances. The observed administrative cost of an underground-bank route, before criminal exposure and before confiscation of illegal gains, is therefore roughly 7% to 12% of the amount moved.

observations.finding: Splitting other people's annual quotas is charged as evasion of FX supervision under Art.39, not merely as a quota breach.
observations.evidence: Every published splitting case cites Measures Art.7 as the rule breached and Regulation Art.39 as the penalty basis, with an order to repatriate the funds within a time limit.
observations.significance: The repatriation order is the commercially decisive part: the money does not stay offshore. A fine is payable and the funds are ordered back.

observations.evidence: A bank was fined and had RMB 1,000,000 confiscated for processing split purchases across 303 individuals' quotas; another RMB 800,000 for processing payments against false bills of lading.
observations.significance: Banks have their own exposure, which explains the conservative and inconsistent authenticity reviews individual customers experience at the counter.

observations.finding: The criminal threshold for illegal FX dealing is low relative to the sums in question.
observations.evidence: Fashi [2019] No.1 sets 'serious circumstances' at an illegal business amount of RMB 5,000,000 or illegal gains of RMB 100,000, and 'especially serious' at RMB 25,000,000 or RMB 500,000.
observations.significance: A single underground-bank transaction moving a mid-six-figure USD sum crosses the criminal threshold. The administrative fines above are the better outcome, not the expected one.
